core.title: Pick exactly one optimization dimension per DESIRED OUTCOME
core.given: A DESIRED OUTCOME is being authored or revised from a user's intent
core.when: the planner states what the user wants to optimize
core.then: Select exactly one optimization dimension (the core metric the user wants to optimize) from: Time, Effort, Likelihood, Frequency, Quantity/Amount, Financial Value.
prefer: Match the user's intent to a dimension via its keywords; decompose into dimension/actor/action/object using the description and rationale.

Time = duration/speed/waiting/delay/rework (performer's most finite resource); Effort = physical or cognitive load (muscular force or concentration/learning/decision-making); Likelihood = probability of an outcome (predictability, control, success vs error).

Frequency = rate of occurrence (reduce repetitive/non-value-added tasks); Quantity/Amount = volume of a resource consumed or produced (optimize inputs/outputs); Financial Value = monetary impact (cost, revenue, opportunity cost).
Shape like: 'Time: minimize onboarding time', 'Likelihood: increase usable experiment results', 'Effort: reduce mental effort to find a bug'.
avoid: Assigning two or more dimensions to one DESIRED OUTCOME; split the DESIRED OUTCOME instead.
Using a dimension outside the six-value catalog.
core.why: One dimension names the core metric to optimize; statement templates and acceptance metrics derive from it, so mixing breaks that mapping.
evidence: Each DESIRED OUTCOME has exactly one dimension, and it is one of the six catalog names.
Reviewer confirms the DESIRED OUTCOME statement's optimization verb/object matches the chosen dimension's keywords and description.
verification: Structural check: parse each DESIRED OUTCOME plan artifact (located through the profile's plan-artifact paths and name patterns) and flag a DESIRED OUTCOME with zero dimensions, more than one dimension, or a dimension value outside the six-name catalog.

The dimension catalog is structured as name -> {keywords, description} and is exposed as the shared catalog term 'dimension' with label 'Dimensions'; the check compares the chosen dimension name against the catalog names.

The structural check does not judge whether the chosen dimension matches the user's intent; that fit is a semantic judgment confirmed by review against the chosen dimension's keywords and description.

values: DESIRED OUTCOME with more than one dimension
DESIRED OUTCOME dimension outside the six-value catalog

fires: Planner writes a new DESIRED OUTCOME and must state what the user wants to optimize.
Planner edits an existing DESIRED OUTCOME statement so that its optimization goal changes.
A DESIRED OUTCOME statement names two metrics (e.g. faster and cheaper) and the planner must choose one.
Planner edits any part of a DESIRED OUTCOME that currently has no dimension, several dimensions, or a dimension outside the catalog.
doesNotFire: Editing a DESIRED OUTCOME's acceptance steps or wording without touching its dimension or optimization goal, when that DESIRED OUTCOME already has exactly one catalog dimension.
Writing code, tests, or docs that are not DESIRED OUTCOME planning artifacts.
Choosing the lens for a DESIRED OUTCOME (covered by the lens-selection rule of the same family).

profileRequirements.meaning: Where plan artifacts (DESIRED OUTCOMES) live, so the rule's plan-artifact activation fact and the structural check can locate DESIRED OUTCOME files; the core defers exact location globs to the profile because they depend on repo topology.
Name patterns that identify DESIRED OUTCOME plan-artifact files regardless of the directory they sit in.

bunOnly.reason: Finding ids of this rule's detector are realization details; the core keeps the three findings as generic descriptions so another stack can name them differently.

neutralityNotes: This convention is methodology-level, so almost everything carries over verbatim: DESIRED OUTCOME terminology, the six-dimension catalog (including its shared catalog term id 'dimension' and label 'Dimensions', which are neutral metadata carried in the core's verification), the keyword guidance and the examples name no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path. Only two pieces of content were stack-bound. (1) The 'path_glob' activation fact (**/plan/**, **/capabilities/**, **/*.desired outcome.*, **/*desired outcome*.yaml) has no neutral fact type; it became a file_kind=plan_artifact fact whose exact locations and name patterns come from the profile keys roles.plan_artifact.path and suffix.plan_artifact. (2) The detector's finding ids in activation.facts[3] are realization identifiers; they are bunOnly, and the core's verification names the check generically. Two topology phrasings were generalized without changing scope: 'for a product capability' in fires[0] (product capability is the stack's layout term for a product slice) was dropped, and the sibling rule id 'planner.desired-outcome.lens-selection' in doesNotFire[2] became 'the lens-selection rule of the same family'. No exceptions existed to preserve (unless is empty), and nothing was added.
